claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform fine lamellar microstructure containing FCC and B2 lamellae.
The starting alloy's strength and plasticity are below industrial fastener requirements.
The proposed intervention is ageing at approximately 650 degrees Celsius for 2–6 hours under inert atmosphere followed by rapid quenching.
Ageing at approximately 650 degrees Celsius for 2–6 hours will induce L12 precipitation in the FCC lamellae.
The proposed ageing and quenching treatment will preserve the original fine FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The treatment will produce a uniform dispersion of coherent nanoscale L12 precipitates within the FCC lamellae.
The coherent nanoscale L12 precipitates obstruct dislocations through the Orowan bypass mechanism.
L12 precipitation produces precipitation strengthening.
The precipitate/matrix interfaces act as barriers to creep deformation.
The precipitate/matrix interfaces reduce sites vulnerable to corrosion.
The precipitates stabilize phase boundaries during cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
The aged alloy will have greater yield strength than the as-cast alloy.
The aged alloy will have greater room-temperature creep resistance than the as-cast alloy.
The aged alloy will have greater resistance to corrosive damage than the as-cast alloy.
The aged alloy will have improved durability under cyclic extreme-temperature fluctuations.
Ductility will remain acceptable because the L12 precipitates are coherent.
Testing at 900 degrees Celsius in a Na2SO4/NaCl molten-salt environment is an applicable hot-corrosion boundary for AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The proposed treatment is applicable to long-term mechanical and fatigue loading.
The long-term stability of the L12 precipitates under the proposed service conditions is uncertain.

Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement of more than approximately 10–20% in yield strength, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance, or loss of ductility below acceptable limits, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The precipitates are specified as coherent and nanoscale, but the mechanism assigns them to Orowan bypass. The cited strengthening record states that small coherent precipitates are normally sheared, whereas Orowan bypass applies to other precipitate conditions.
